audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dell'1.75%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.10%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha registrato un rialzo dell'1.20%, il VIX è sceso del 2.56%. L'oro si mantiene sopra i 4879 dollari l'oncia, in rialzo del 1.97%. Il petrolio è in calo del 9.07% a 90.38 dollari.

La situazione in Iran continua a tenere banco, con un'attenzione crescente sui mercati finanziari. La BCE ha recentemente rilasciato il tasso di deposito al 2.00%.

I dati macro USA più recenti mostrano un CPI YoY al 3.3%, un Core CPI YoY al 2.7% e un tasso di disoccupazione al 4.3%. La prossima uscita importante è il PIL QoQ USA previsto per il 29 aprile.

Mentre le borse mondiali osservano la consueta pausa festiva, i riflettori restano accesi sul comparto digitale, che opera 24 ore su 24. Il Bitcoin è sceso dello 0.56% a 75,304 dollari. L'Indice di Fear & Greed è a 27, in zona Fear.

[{'bitcoin': 'Bitcoin scende del 2.22% e si posiziona sotto i settantacinquemila dollari. Flussi ETF in positivo con un afflusso giornaliero di 663.9 milioni di dollari.'}, {'altcoins': 'Ethereum in calo del 3.58% a 2319 dollari, Solana scende del 3.92% a 84.94 dollari e BNB perde il 3.53% a 620.92 dollari.'}, {'sentiment': 'Il Fear & Greed Index è a 27, in zona Fear.'}]

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, e monitorate le notizie relative alle principali società quotate. Un saluto da Price Alert, arrivederci alla prossima puntata. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 
  Traditional markets are closed for the weekend. 
  In their last close, Asia finished mixed: Nikkei dropped 1.75% to 58,476, while Shanghai edged down 0.10% to 4051.43. 
  This sets a cautious tone for the European and US outlook.

  Focusing on the previous close for Western markets: 
  S&P 500 rose 1.20% to 7126.06, VIX dropped 2.56% to 17.48, and DXY fell 0.12% to 98.10. 
  Gold surged 1.97% to hold above $4879.60/oz, and oil prices plummeted 9.07% to $90.38.

  On the macro front, attention is on geopolitical tensions. 
  The IMF gathering in Washington discussed the Iran war's impact on the global economy. 
  Japan's debt interest payments are forecast to triple by fiscal 2035 due to rate rises.

  While traditional markets are closed, digital assets remain active. 
  Bitcoin is down 0.56% to $75,304. 
  Ethereum, Solana, and BNB are also seeing declines. 
  The Fear & Greed Index stands at 27, indicating fear in the market.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin is down two point two two percent, trading below seventy five thousand dollars. The ETF daily net inflow was six hundred sixty three point nine million dollars.

In the altcoin space, Ethereum is down three point five eight percent to two thousand three hundred nineteen dollars, Solana down three point nine two percent to eighty four point nine four dollars, and Binance Coin down three point five three percent to six hundred twenty point nine two dollars.

The Fear & Greed Index is at twenty seven, classified as Fear.

Thanks for tuning in and we'll see you tomorrow. Have a great day and goodbye from Price Alert.

articles.title: Implementing the digital euro project
articles.snippet: The European Central Bank (ECB) is working on a digital version of the euro, a project started back in 2020 that is coming closer to fruition as the enabling EU legislation progresses. The ECB has designed a digital equivalent of cash, aimed at complementing physical euros for day-to-day payments. Its approach may be compared and contrasted with the US Federal Reserve’s reluctance to introduce a digital dollar and with the People’s Bank of China’s definition of the digital yuan largely as a bank deposit. Has the ECB’s rationale for the digital euro evolved over time, from a response to tech…

articles.title: Book launch: World War Trade: Conflict, Containment, and the Emergent World Trading Order
articles.snippet: Globalization is not dying. It is being rebuilt. When the United States and China weaponized trade in 2025, many feared the collapse of the global economy. Markets plunged, supply chains fractured, and policymakers spoke openly of economic warfare. But the collapse never came. In his new book, World War Trade, published by the Centre for Economic Policy Research, Richard Baldwin argues that the real story is not the conflict between superpowers but how the rest of the world responded. Through quiet restraint, strategic adaptation, and a wave of new trade agreements, countries representing the…

articles.title: Traders placed over $1bn in perfectly timed bets on the Iran war. What is going on?
articles.snippet: Suspicious wagers on the US-Israel war in Iran are creating huge windfalls and raising concerns among lawmakers Sixteen bets made $100,000 each accurately predicting the timing of the US airstrikes against Iran on 27 February. Later, a single user would make over $550,000 after betting that Ayatollah Ali Khamenei would topple, just moments before his assassination by Israeli forces. On 7 April, right before Donald Trump announced a temporary ceasefire with Iran, traders bet $950m that oil prices would come down. They did. These bets and other well-timed wagers accurately predicted the precise timing of major developments in the US-Israel war with Iran, creating huge windfalls and raising concerns among lawmakers and experts over potential insider trading. Continue reading...

articles.title: Europe’s Energy Problem Isn’t the Transition—It’s That Europe Never Finished It
articles.snippet: By now, a familiar narrative has returned to Europe’s energy debate. The transition, we are told, went too far, too fast, and too blindly. Politicians chased climate headlines, imposed unrealistic targets, burdened households with costs, and pushed industry toward the exit. It is a compelling story. It is also the wrong one. Europe’s real mistake was not moving too quickly on clean energy. It was moving halfway. We invested in renewable generation, but underinvested in the grids, storage, flexibility, and electrification required to…
